### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c9ba22622f9a1ea473a164421d52f934e095919` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5277954388483846baa7c46e0906a38978214d0a` — the merge of head `a6b929fa399206ea8c8353f1c37902fc4cfe7945` into base `5c9ba22622f9a1ea473a164421d52f934e095919`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5277954388483846baa7c46e0906a38978214d0a && git checkout 5277954388483846baa7c46e0906a38978214d0a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c9ba22622f9a1ea473a164421d52f934e095919 a6b929fa399206ea8c8353f1c37902fc4cfe7945 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c9ba22622f9a1ea473a164421d52f934e095919 && git merge --no-ff a6b929fa399206ea8c8353f1c37902fc4cfe7945

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c9ba22622f9a1ea473a164421d52f934e095919
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a6b929fa399206ea8c8353f1c37902fc4cfe7945`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/execution.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/run-status-liveness.test.ts, packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-automation-run.object.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-result-status.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json, .changeset/25325-execution-status-missed.md

Face: published schema (`reviewFace` hits `packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts`). The three prose-face paths (the changeset body and the two regenerated references) remain the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #25325 (body, claim 6356112178, os-dev-report 6356650534); on its parent #25235 the ruling 6353729816 and the hand-off answers 6354378101 and 6355021401; PR #25363's body, file list and net diff against merge-base 69913f8ba at head a6b929fa3; the 47 check-runs on that head. Read-only shape held: the cited files were read from the committed tree at the head, nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept set: `ExecutionStatus` goes from nine to ten members, `'missed'` appended last; the first eight are unchanged, `options[8]` is `refused`, `options.at(-1)` is `missed`. Right. The order pin in `execution.test.ts` moves exactly that way and gains a negative control (`skipped` is refused). Right.
2. TSDoc claims against the schema at this head: `ExecutionLogSchema` has `startedAt` required, `completedAt` / `durationMs` / `refusalMessage` optional, `steps` a required array, and no top-level `error` (errors live on `steps[].error`). The PR's correction of the card's wording (`error` absent on the stored row, not on the log) is right. `sys_automation_run` carries `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`, `error` and `refusal_message` columns. Right.
3. Public surface that widens by construction: `ListRunsRequestSchema.status` is `ExecutionStatus.optional()` (`automation-api.zod.ts:692`) and the REST boundary reads `ExecutionStatus.options` (`runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3657`), so `?status=missed` is declared and accepted in the same stroke; `automation-api.zod.test.ts:719` pins the two sets equal and `automation-runs-query-validation.test.ts:445` drives every member through the boundary. Right; no re-listed copy exists to drift.
4. Surfaces claimed untouched: `AutomationResult.status` and `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data.status` stay five (`automation-result-status.pin.test.ts` unchanged, and it deliberately pins no relation to `ExecutionStatus`); `JobExecutionStatus` (`system/job.zod.ts:501`) is a separate vocabulary. `client` and `service-automation` `listRuns` use the type only as a parameter. Right.
5. Totality sweep: the only map keyed by `ExecutionStatus` in `packages/**` is `RUN_STATUS_LIVENESS` (`approval-service.ts:535`, `as const satisfies` a Record over the enum), which gains `missed: 'terminal'`; `run-status-liveness.test.ts:171` compares its keys with `.options` in both directions and drives every member through the real sweep (Test Core green). No exhaustive switch exists. Right. `terminal` is the right class: the member is documented terminal, and an approval pending on a row that never ran must be swept, not kept alive.
6. Declared-but-inert window: `sys_automation_run.status` options (`sys-automation-run.object.ts:201`), the retention `onlyWhen` set (`:67`) and `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` (`engine.ts:1637`) are hand lists, not total maps, and do not widen here, by design: ruling 6353729816 item 4 widens them together with the producer in the services PR, the `refused` precedent (#14945 then #15788) and the ADR-0078 condition recorded at `sys-automation-run.object.ts:191-199` are the same shape. Until then a `missed` row is refused as `invalid_option` and `?status=missed` answers an empty list, both loud. Right.
7. Cross-lane hunk: the one `plugin-approvals` line is required for the member to compile (`satisfies`), was asked for by the services seat (addendum 6354069893, confirmed on #25235 by 6354378101 and 6355021401) and is declared in the PR body under `domain:services`. Right. `api-surface/automation.json` records `ExecutionStatus` by name only, so no snapshot regeneration is owed (`check:api-surface` green); no `authorable-surface` entry names the enum, consistent with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
8. Prose: outside the two regenerated references no hand-written page under `content/docs/**` enumerates the run statuses (one v17.5 release note mentions `cancelled` / `timed_out` historically). Nothing is left stale; `check:generated`, `check:docs` and Build Docs are green.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand line-initial on the PR body and the changeset. One changeset at `patch` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, the two published packages the diff moves. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the kind alone and `none` takes `patch`; a run-row and wire value is nothing a metadata author writes. Matches. Title `feat(spec)` without `!`: nothing accepted before is refused. Matches. Check Changeset green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none (os-dev-report 6356650534).
- Dev flag, producer-less until the services PR for #25235: answered by ① 6. The services side is parked on `Restart-when: git grep "'missed'" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts hits` (6354378101) and resumes when this merges. No action here.
- Dev flag, correction to the card's wording on `error`: answered by ① 2; the TSDoc is right and the card's sentence was the loose one.
- Claim deviation, branch `claude/project-thread-7afd2e` in place of `claude/issue-25325-*`: named in claim 6356112178; the claim check and the single-writer check are green on this head. Not a contract matter.
- Not this PR's, left where the ruling put them: the objectui run-status renderer (ruling item 8, the services seat's ACCEPT) and the maintainer flag on bounding `missed` rows tighter than the per-flow cap (ruling item 5 g).
- Checks: 47 check-runs on the head, each `success` or an opt-in / path-filtered `skipped` (Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, dogfood shards). Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Lint, Type Check, Build Core and Test Core are all green.
